reason: Wording confirmed verbatim in Project Gutenberg ebook 1325 (Twenty Years at Hull-House, Chapter VI) and independently in the 1893 first printing of the paper (Philanthropy and Social Progress: Seven Essays, Crowell, 1893, essay I, archive.org scan philanthropyand00huntgoog): the good we secure for ourselves is precarious and uncertain, is floating in mid-air, until it is secured for all of us and incorporated into our common life. Two caveats, neither fatal. First, in both editions this is the last of a series of that-clauses in one long sentence (that the good we secure...), so the shipped line raises the initial letter to a capital; every word is hers in order and nothing is minted, but the editor should know the line is a lifted clause, not a sentence of the edition. Second, Addams introduces the chapter as parts of a lecture I delivered in Plymouth in 1892; it was, however, first published as an essay in the 1893 Crowell volume and again in the 1910 memoir, and the shipped tag Essay fits that published form, so it is not the Makers' oratory. Not shipped, not near a shipped line; Addams new to the year, not banned. Source line leads with the name, no dash, 118 characters; the chapter head in the book reads Subjective Necessity for Social Settlements (the contents page carries the article The), a trivial variance.
